Dr. Phil McGraw faces a wrongful termination lawsuit from his longtime publicist alleging anti-gay discrimination, following the bankruptcy liquidation of his network Merit Street Media.

The Bright Side:
Formal legal discovery and judicial oversight force internal corporate practices and messaging logs out of behind-the-scenes ambiguity and into public record.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error swaps corporate morality (WHAT) with administrative control (WHO). Shielding operations behind mandatory faith pledges and deleting evidence shifts liability onto subordinates.

Social Physics Analysis:
Using startup reorganization as a pretext for selective exclusion isolates workers and concentrates authority. When transparency fails, post-hoc justifications replace upfront equity.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between public ethics assertions and evidence deletion, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil, driving organizational breakdown.

The Unavoidable Truth: Bankruptcy proceedings uncovered deleted evidence and hidden communications.

The Unavoidable Lie: Staffing exclusion was merely a routine startup hiatus.

Alethekanon:
Court findings of spoliation in bankruptcy court undermine corporate defenses of fair practice and neutral staffing decisions.

Awwthekanon:
Everyone deserves to be judged on their professional merit and dedication, not excluded or pushed aside because of who they are.

Brothekanon:
Deleting text messages during a bankruptcy case while making employees sign faith cards is a bold corporate strategy that usually backfires in court.

Spirithekanon:
"There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, or hidden that will not be made known." (Luke 12:2) — FAIL (Transparency Axis)
Concealing facts and excluding workers violates fundamental ethical duties.
